# 1.2.69 - rolls and writes under test

The fifteenth stage on the way to 1.3.0 (E33), released on its own. It
puts what 1.2.68 built under test: a new scenario plays every legal road
of a player's roll and sheet, then changes sent from a player's browser
console, and the GMs' record now names who sent what it would not take.
With it come the GM's public roll, a Monocub's abilities as one table
and a private roll that keeps its whisper.

## Before installing

1. **Every browser at the table should run 1.2.69.** A Monocub's
   Confusion now reaches the GM as a request with a new name
   (`monocub.ability`, was `monocub.meddle`). Where a player's browser
   and the primary GM's run the two versions side by side, the GM's
   browser does not know the request and the Confusion goes unanswered
   (read in the code).
2. **A macro naming the Monocub's old functions breaks.**
   `game.drpg.performMeddle`, `meddleDialog`, `meddleTargets` and
   `resolveMeddle` are gone. In their place:
   `performCubAbility(actor, "meddle", { targetId, choice })`, with
   `choice` "help" or "hinder"; `cubAbilityDialog(actor, "meddle")`;
   `cubTargets(actor, "meddle")`; and on the GM `cubAbilityOnGm`, which
   throws its own roll (`resolveMeddle` took a total).
   `game.drpg.isSilenced` still answers the crime-witness marker, as an
   alias; `isCrimeSilenced` and `isCallSilenced` (the Despair Call
   "Silence") are new.
3. **No new migration step and no new setting.** The hint of the world
   setting "Force private player rolls" now names the one roll it leaves
   public, the GM's Public roll.

## At the table, as the GM

- **There is nothing new to do.** In the harness, every legal road of a
  player's roll and sheet - eleven, from a Search to a Level Up, a
  Monocub's Confusion and the killer's incident rolls among them - raised
  nothing: no roll flagged, no write put back or flagged, no card to the
  GMs, no refusal, no "not counted" line (scenario 83; a table's evening
  is not measured yet).
- **`game.drpg.sheetWrites()` names who sent what was not taken.** Three
  new kinds of row, each naming the player Foundry names as the sender
  or the author, with a `what` column: `refused`, a Daggerheart request
  about a student or its items that the primary GM's browser refused;
  `forged`, a message a player's browser wrote with a flag only a GM's
  browser writes; `rewrite`, a roll's dice a player rewrote, put back,
  once per message and player (read in the code). A `refused` or
  `forged` row counts the same trace from the same player about the
  same student again within half a minute (`times`) instead of adding
  one; it keeps the changes each named, up to twelve, and a `forged`
  row lists the messages it counted. When a player's own roll the GM
  did not draw earns Hope, the gain stands on a `covered` row naming
  that roll's message: one roll covers one gain. Tested in tier 2: "a
  player's message with the drawn flag is not read as drawn and awards
  nothing and is named once", "a refused relay write on another's
  student leaves a row naming its sender" and "a rewrite put back
  leaves a row naming the player".
- **A message a player's browser writes with a GM's flags counts for
  nothing.** No browser reads it as a roll the GM drew: it awards
  nothing, is never on the card of rolls made with no GM, is never
  granted, and no Reroll reads it as drawn. The GMs are whispered once
  per message. The primary GM's browser names it when it is posted, when
  such a flag is added to it later, and, for one posted while no GM was
  connected, when the primary GM's world loads.
- **The GM's public roll.** With rolls forced private, the **Public
  roll** tile in the GM panel's Right now group (a formula and a
  flavour; the tile read in the code) and
  `game.drpg.publicRoll(formula, { flavor })` throw the one roll every
  player reads - a vote's tie, Monokuma's lottery - speaking as the GM,
  never as a token the GM has selected. A GM's own `/r` still goes to
  the GMs; a player's message carrying the public roll's flag stays
  private and is a `forged` row.
- **A statistic thrown with no GM is a reaction.** Shift-clicked on a
  sheet while no GM is connected, it is now thrown as a reaction, as one
  clicked through its window already was, and when granted moves neither
  its Hope nor, on a Fear result, the GMs' Despair. Until now it was
  thrown as an action, and Grant all paid what an action would.
- **A silent GM, or one who leaves, now measured.** In the harness
  (scenario 15; the draw's wait in tier 2), a drawn roll whose GM is
  connected but never answers ends after 30 seconds as not answered: the
  action comes back, nothing is posted, the player is told once and a
  later answer plays nothing. A GM leaving while a player's Search picker
  is open refuses the draw the same way, and the player is told it waits
  for a GM. There is still no Cancel button while a roll waits
  (deliberately left).

## Changed

- **One road for a player's own writes.** Every document write a
  player's browser makes on its own student now takes the road the
  primary GM's browser judges, naming its reason; the suite's census of
  the module's document writes (R220) fails unless each is on it, on a
  GM's own road, or not about a student. `sheetWrites()` now names the
  reason on a free Move given back (`refund`) and on armed Calls spent
  (`call`). `game.drpg.syncStates`, the module's Search settlement and
  the Contraband Call act only on a GM's browser, where play already ran
  them (read in the code).
- **A Call's bonus reaches the roll.** The bonus a Call arms - a
  Confusion's +1 - is written read-only into the roll window's bonus
  field and now travels with the roll, counted without a flag; until
  now, on the harness's stand-in of the window, it stayed out of the
  roll the window sent and the GMs were whispered about an honest
  roll. A Call taken back while the window is open leaves the field
  empty. Measured on that stand-in only (tier 2: "a Meddle's +1 the
  window writes is in the roll it sends and scored without an alarm").
- **The dice a roll claims.** A Hope or Fear die at other faces, in
  another number or with a modifier of its own, and an advantage die at
  other faces than the GMs' rules give, are named `dice` on the roll's
  flags, with one whisper to the GMs; the GM throws its own dice either
  way. The flag's label reads "dice", no longer "extra dice" (tier 2: "a
  d20 Hope die on a drawn roll is not counted and the GMs are told
  once", and its Fear twin).
- **A private roll keeps its whisper.** The module writes a private
  roll's readers first and on their own, and its mode after and apart,
  so where writing the mode fails the whisper stands. The mode is
  written only where the readers are the GMs and the roller; a wider
  list, such as a Monocub's room or a GM's roll from a student's sheet,
  keeps its whisper and the mode it came with. Nothing in the module
  reads Foundry 13's roll-mode constant any more, and a roll's message
  no longer carries the `core.rollMode` flag.
- **An incident's write that fails is put back.** The incident is
  written in two parts, the cast first. When the second fails, the cast
  is put back to what it was and the error goes on to the write's
  caller - and if the put-back fails as well, its own error is on the
  GM's console; the incident's next write runs as before. A crisis
  action whose turn could not pass still closes its receipt, so its
  Reroll can take it back.
- **A Monocub's abilities are one table.** Confusion is the one row of
  `MONOCUB.abilities` in config.mjs, with one executor, one picker and
  one request to the GM. The GM's browser throws the 2d12, checks the
  target once more and scores it; a refusal is told to the Monocub and
  refunds nothing, as before. A Monocub marked as a crime witness still
  lands Confusion: the marker is information only. A second ability is
  one row and one resolver (read in the code).
- **`perf()` reports a drawn roll's round trip.** A block, "Rolls the GM
  drew": of the last fifty draws this browser took part in, how many,
  the median and the slowest - on the roller from asking to the dice
  shown, on the drawing GM from the packet in to the answer out. A
  refused or unanswered draw is not kept, and nothing is sent or stored
  (read in the code); the harness counts the draws and their order,
  never a time.

## Known gaps

- Two of Foundry's stamps on a player's message are assumed, not yet
  read at a table: its author, which names the player on a row and
  decides whether a message counts as one a GM drew, and its creation
  time. By that time the primary GM's world, when it loads, passes over
  a message older than a day, and by the date its author wrote where
  there is none (read in the code, not tested); in the harness one its
  author dated two days back is still named (tier 2).
- A player's change to the dice of a roll the GM drew is refused by
  Foundry on that player's page before any GM's browser hears of it:
  nothing changes, and no row can name it (scenario 83, on the
  harness's model of Foundry; at a table, LIVE-E33-02, not yet run).
- Rolls the GM does not draw - with no GM, on a Daggerheart build whose
  rolls stay in the players' browsers, and Daggerheart's item and damage
  rolls - are still not held to the GMs' list (deliberately left); where
  one earns Hope, one roll covers one gain.
- A message a player's browser wrote with a GM's flags stays in the
  chat, counting for nothing, until a GM deletes it, and every browser
  handles it as that player's own roll (read in the code at each place
  that asks). A player's own roll is made private by that player's
  browser, which can leave it public (deliberately left).
- A `rewrite` row is one per message and player and is not folded
  (read in the code); a run of them over many messages is not measured.
  A row keeps at most twelve changes and twelve items (chosen; no test
  reaches either cap), and how far a long session's day of rows grows
  is not measured.
- A roll sent from a window left open while a GM changed the faces of
  the Hope or Fear die is named `dice` too, with a whisper to the GMs
  (read in the code, not measured).
- The harness applies a roll's mode before the module's hook; whether
  Foundry 14 does so before or after is not read at a table. If after, a
  roll whose readers are wider than the GMs and the roller follows the
  mode it was sent with, and a GM's roll aimed by its mode alone is
  handled as one with no mode (read in the code).
- A formula Foundry's own check refuses is not modelled for the public
  roll: the harness lacks that check, and the module's catch around the
  throw is read in the code, not driven. Dice So Nice on a public roll
  is not modelled headless.
- On the roller, `perf()`'s round trip ends when the dice are shown,
  Dice So Nice's animation included where it runs (read in the code).
- A GM leaving while a player's roll window is open, rather than a
  Search's picker, ends the draw as one with no GM (read in the code,
  not driven).
- When an incident's write fails, what came before it stands: a crisis
  action's effect, with its actor keeping the turn, and a close's
  earlier steps, a self-inflicted death among them; a put-back that
  fails itself leaves the cast a step ahead (each read in the code).
  What a put-back sends the participants is read in the code, not
  measured.

## Checked

- The headless suite, run as `npm test` on this release's code (commit
  6dfdca8: the tree that ships but for the version stamps, these notes,
  the ledger's rows, CLAUDE.md's suite line, the incident's row of the
  flow registry and the flow one phase of scenario 83 is tagged with): 937
  passed, 0 failed, 17 skipped (863 at 1.2.68). New in the suite: R291,
  R300, R301, R302 and R303, and the tier-2 tests of each change. The
  scenarios: 18 of 18 green; 72's three expected reds stand (S17-31 until
  E43, a Foundry limit, S17-64 until E60). The suite takes about 33
  minutes on the test machine, the whole of `npm test` 55; the harness now
  gives the suite 72 minutes, and CI's suite job 80.
- At the stage's second and third whole-chain checkpoints the suite
  read one test red and then two; each was the test's own reading, not
  the module's, and both are fixed: a later Reroll's test stood in a
  player's message carrying flags only the GM's browser writes, which
  the module stopped honouring earlier in this stage, and `perf()`'s
  test counted round trips by the length of a list kept at fifty.
  Scenario 30's pair of counts, which landed three times in an order
  that measured nothing, is thrown again, up to three times.
- The Polish file's prose check: 497 of 497 strings covered, missing 0,
  extra 0.
- Before this commit, the stage's eight verify sentences and four
  doneWhen clauses were each matched to the test or scenario check that
  answers them: eight in full by the suite and the scenarios above, four
  in part. Two halves only a table can answer: scenario 83 through the
  local gate, and a measured `perf()` baseline (LIVE-E33-01 and -05).
  Two clauses describe what the stage did not build: a waiting action
  roll that can be cancelled (with no GM an action is refused before
  anything is paid, and one whose GM goes silent ends at 30 seconds),
  and a silenced Monocub's Confusion refused (the plan dropped it; a
  crime witness's Confusion lands, and the suite says so). The same
  reading found no tier 0 or 1 test guarding the path with no GM; R303
  is that guard: it reads in the code that an action's roll is refused
  and any other roll stamped and moving nothing, and drives the draw's
  30-second wait with stand-ins.
  These notes and the changed handbook lines were then read once more
  against those tests and logs: of the notes, seven sentences were given
  a label saying what they rest on and seven were rewritten to what the
  logs support; six handbook lines, each in English and Polish, now say
  whether they were measured, and a seventh names only the traces it is
  true of.
- Daggerheart 2.10.5's own roll and dice classes now run in the harness,
  copied unchanged as its GM-side handler already was: a roll's build,
  its dice and their faces, the resource step and a live reroll, under
  the module's roll-window hooks on a stand-in of Daggerheart's window,
  whose form, chat card, triggers and countdowns do not run. So run,
  before this release's changes, a Confusion's +1 stayed out of the roll
  the window sent and a d20 Hope or Fear die raised no flag.
- A new scenario, 83, in the ci and local-gate layers, plays the eleven
  legal roads above from each player's own page, then thirteen changes
  sent from a player's browser console, each read on all four browsers:
  each put back or never applied but the one Hope a roll the GM does not
  draw may earn (Known gaps), and each named with that player - on the
  GMs' record or, for the two crisis packets, in the GM's console
  warning - counted exactly, but the one Foundry refuses on the player's
  page. It takes about three minutes (155 to 176 seconds where this stage
  timed it) and declares a bound of seven, as scenario 30 now does.
- Tier 2 draws every entry of the GMs' list of what may add to a drawn
  roll, and every branch of its situation entry - nineteen fixtures -
  with its source and without, on the same dice and on Daggerheart's own
  roll classes: each moves the roll by what its rule gives and raises
  nothing, but for a hindering Call the roll left out, named as its
  rule says. Claims off the list are each not counted, and the GMs are
  told once. R291 fails the suite when an entry or a branch has no
  fixture, or a fixture names none.
- The incident's grid draws crisis rolls on the GMs' record and rerolls
  them from there - a Strike whose Reroll misses, a critical Strike on
  each of the killer's picks, an accomplice's death the GMs keep (DM20,
  DM21, DM22, TP15) - each settled once, on its record's last version
  (I15); and it refuses an incident's writes on purpose (XI08, XI09): the
  incident is left before or after, never half (I16), and a failed
  put-back's error reaches the GM's console (I17).
- An independent review in two rounds (security, and whether the change
  is correct and its tests measure); its findings were fixed in three
  commits after the first round and four after the second, and one more
  after the verify reading above adds R303.
- Not checked in a real Foundry yet: scenario 83 through the local gate
  on a Foundry 14 sandbox with Daggerheart 2.6.5 and 2.10.x and the real
  roll window (`sandbox-83-roll-integrity`, not run); "Reroll action
  roll" and the die button as a player; the whispers and a roll's mode on
  Foundry 14 with rolls forced private, a Monocub's roll with its room
  and a GM's roll from a student's sheet among them, and Dice So Nice
  only for their readers; the GM's public roll with a student's token
  selected; `perf()`'s round trip on a player and on the GM, in both
  themes (also item 96); Confusion from the table and its +1 on
  Daggerheart's own window; a GM leaving or reloading while a player's
  Search is drawn; a crisis Strike and a critical Strike rerolled from
  the GMs' record; the author and the time Foundry stamps on a player's
  message - the audit's live checks, section 9.2, items 125 to 134

  and did not run for this release.
